MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING
  October 17, 2022

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 7:10 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers, 4045
  Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, Pepperwood Park and Peter Weber
  Equestrian Center (Park Tours) by CHAIR CIAROLLA.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CIAROLLA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Ciarolla, Romanelli, McCormick, and Retz

  Commissioners Absent:  Bain and Persichina

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 6, 2022

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  September 6, 2022.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  B.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 19, 2022

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  September 19, 2022.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
October 17, 2022
   There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA GIRLS SOFTBALL LEAGUE REQUEST TO
  INSTALL ONE UTILITY DUGOUT BOX AT HIGHRIDGE PARK

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the written
  report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if there were any more groups that may request
  more storage items at the park. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas
  responded that they are currently the only group that uses Highridge Park softball
  field. She also stated that they have one storage unit already at the park, but they
  understand the Commission does not want multiple storage units at the park. This
  smaller utility box allows for storage of smaller items without adding another larger
  storage shed. COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if the utility box would impede the use
  of the dugout. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the utility box is
  a smaller box like you would have in a pick-up truck to hold smaller items like bases
  and marking paint. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if there is already
  cement located at the installation site. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith
  stated yes cement is already present at the location.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked what guidance staff was looking from the
  Commission. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that the
  Commission could share concerns or feedback regarding painting the unit or
  keeping it as shown in the picture attached to the report. COMMISSIONER RETZ
  recommended painting it a color that allowed the box to blend in as much as
  possible but will leave the color to the guidance of the staff. COMMISSIONER
  POPE agreed with COMMISSIONER RETZ regarding the paint color adding it
  would be best to keep with the current standards throughout all the parks and
  remain consistent.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI to:

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
October 17, 2022
   APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF THE UTILITY BOX BY THE PVP
  GIRLS SOFTBALL LEAGUE AS REPORTED WITH GUIDANCE FROM
  STAFF TO ENSURE THAT THE BOX IS PAINTED TO CITY STANDARDS.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  B.  SILVER SPUR LITTLE LEAGUE REQUEST

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a brief overview of the written report.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that there is an issue right now that Little
  League has not been keeping up the maintenance of the batting cages recently. He
  stated that the subcommittee would like to see better maintenance and upkeep of
  the current facilities prior to the approval of the updates proposed to the batting
  cages. He also stated that the League appears pleased with the cooperation
  between the City and the League, and that the installation of a new scoreboard is
  an example of the positive relationship.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that the recommendation from staff is appropriate
  regarding the installation of the new scoreboard. She also stated the upgrade to the
  batting cages could be a reasonable addition but should be looked further. She
  noted that Ernie Howlett is a public park, not a school or private league facility, so
  there should be some limits to enhancements to facilities.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ asked if Little League is still allowed to have practices with
  a pitching coach or hitting coach during their off-season leagues. ACM Davis stated
  that staff has informed Little League there are no practices allowed during AYSO
  field permit use due to safety concerns. She stated that staff thought they were
  working together last season but later discovered that AYSO had decided not to
  hold practices and games due to the safety concerns. Thus, the City decided to
  maintain the past practice of the in-season sport having priority of the fields. She
  also commented that they do have usage of the batting cages at any time as the
  cages are their exclusive-use facility. COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she had
  the same question at a subcommittee meeting but realized that it does make sense
  due to the size and limitation of the park to limit the park use to one sport at a time.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  POPE to:

  APPROVE THE INSTALLATION OF THE NEW SCOREBOARD BUT
  TABLE THE BATTING CAGE UPDATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
October 17, 2022
   C.  2022 CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief update of the written report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted that when volunteering at the ticket booth he
  received questions regarding where certain events and activities were located so
  he suggested having a map at the ticket booth to assist in answering those
  questions.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that the 2021 costs and the 2022 costs lined
  up with the exception of the increase to the petting zoo and pony rides. Community
  Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the costs did go up even though it was the
  same vendor used in the past due to more time reserved. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI suggested that staff look into some alternative activities or vendors if
  costs remain high or get higher. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated
  that will be looking into different vendors for the petting zoo and pony rides for next
  year’s event.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK stated that the date is a challenge with a lot of
  activities happening in September with different groups and youth sports in the
  area.

  CHAIR CIAROLLA stated that she thought that the event was on a Sunday in the
  past and asked if it be possible to have it on a Sunday instead of a Saturday. ACM
  Davis stated that staff would have to look into the holiday schedule for Sundays and
  with the Empty Saddle Club schedule, as well as any clean up considerations.
  COMMISSIONERS ROMANELLI and POPE shared concerns with the event
  possibly being held on a Sunday. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted that he
  felt Sundays would work better with his family’s schedule. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI stated that we should always try and schedule the event at least a
  week from the birthday of the City as that is what the event is meant to celebrate.

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted the difference in the community organization booths
  from past events. She asked if there was a way to get the community organizations
  more involved with the number of organizations in the area. She stated that there
  may be an opportunity to work with the local youth sports organizations to come out
  and have the kids come in their uniforms with a free activity offer for the kids.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ commented that the QR code on the future event flyers at
  the ticket booth was a great idea and should continue as it made it easier for patrons
  to get easy access to the event’s webpage.

  D.  TRACY AUSTIN UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
October 17, 2022
   Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview. She stated that it
  is always such a great event as families participate together in the doubles teams
  and that helps make the event a wonderful family friendly tournament.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted that George F Canyon had some dead tree
  limbs on the side and a dead Eucalyptus tree that had fallen over in the park. He
  stated that he had taken some pictures to share with staff. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith noted that he would be inspect the area to see what can
  be done.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that Silver Spur Park still looks great. She asked if
  bleachers got placed at Highridge Park. Staff confirmed that the bleachers were
  placed in the past week. She also asked about the planting project at Highridge
  Park. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith stated that they were waiting until the
  completion of the City Hall project before beginning the Highridge Park project.
  ACM Davis added that the Highridge Park project is scheduled to be completed by
  the end of November.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about the restrooms at Ernie Howlett Park
  and if there was any update regarding the renovation of the restrooms as the current
  restrooms seem outdated, especially with the locker space not really being utilized
  anymore. Staff noted that they are currently working on a plan in order to develop
  a renovation project for the restrooms. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked
  when or if the other restrooms by the basketball courts were opened during the
  weekends. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the restrooms by
  the basketball courts were typically only open during special events or if requested
  by AYSO or Little League.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if there has been a study regarding having
  a Chandler Park restroom facility instead of a portable toilet. ACM Davis stated that
  the restrooms in Council Chambers are open and available during normal business
  hours as a restroom facility. Maintenance Superintendent noted that there has not
  been a study regarding restroom facilities at the park and that the current solution
  has been to provide Council Chambers as a restroom facility for the nearby parks.
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if anyone has requested or asked about a
  restroom facility, especially since they were not open during non-business hours.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
October 17, 2022
   Staff confirmed that they had not heard of any issues regarding having the portable
  toilet.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted two concerns that he observed at Ernie
  Howlett Park on Saturday while attending an AYSO games. His first concern was
  two cars were doing donuts in the gravel parking lot. He stated that he tried to video
  the incident, but they were gone before he could get there. His second concern was
  that he noticed that there were a lot of horses backed up on the horse trail up on
  the ridge due to what he assumed was 15-20 people on electronic unicycles. He
  stated that he just wanted to bring it up to see if any equestrians had mentioned
  this issue. CHAIR CIAROLLA asked if anything had been stated in the equestrian
  log. ACM Davis stated that although it is not due to this specific issue the City is
  trying to raise more awareness that bicycles and e-bikes are prohibited on bridle
  trails. ACM Davis stated that anyone can contact the Sheriff regarding any incidents
  or concerns at the parks. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith stated that the
  donuts are an occurrence that happen at the park and the Sheriff will respond.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI added an Adopt a Park comment referencing
  photographs he sent to staff regarding some broken fence rails and the playground
  signage at Rockbluff Park. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about the pole
  play structure on the playground. COMMISSIONERS ROMANELLI and
  MCCORMICK stated that it has handles but is completely stationary and does not
  move. ACM Davis stated that she was looking into that specific piece of play
  equipment and the playground signage and would get back to everyone regarding
  those matters.

  9.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  NOVEMBER MEETING DATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas asked the Commission about the date for
  the upcoming November meeting. She noted that the standard third Monday of the
  month (November 21) fell during the Thanksgiving holiday week and wanted to see
  if the Commission would prefer Monday, November 14 for the meeting in
  November.

  The Commission affirmed and agreed that Monday, November 14 would be best
  for the November meeting.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION ITEMS OF SEPTEMBER 13, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
October 17, 2022
   B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION ITEMS OF SEPTEMBER 27, 2022

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PERIMETER PATHWAY PROJECT

  B.  PARK CAMERAS

  C.  EVENTS AND ACTIVITIES AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

  D.  NAMING OF BUTCHER PARK

  ACM Davis stated that staff were still conducting research on all items and there
  was nothing to report at this time.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR CIAROLLA MOVED TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:58 PM TO THE NEXT PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MEETING ON NOVEMBER 14, 2022, AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH WILL
  BE HELD AT THE CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBER.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CIAROLLA so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  Matt Morrow  Valerie Ciarolla
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission
